name: zc_skeleton_pulse

tests.name: the Dog is wearing Skeleton Flame
the chest was in frame and readable from front, both sides and back
the chest skull is NOT permanently emissive -- it goes out and comes back

detail.note: the fraction of its own cyan the chest loses between beats. Permanently lit reads 0.0 at any brightness, which is what the founder's 'NOT permanently emissive' means in a number. The patch is a chest, not a skull, so it always contains steady soul light as well and the measured depth is far below the 92% the skull is authored at -- what it can prove is that the skull is not constant, and that P03 and P04 tie every other light on the body to it.

tests.name: the head's own light beats with the chest rather than sitting still

detail.note: the eyes and the ear fire ride the same clock at a third of the depth, so this floor is half the chest's on purpose -- the flame must pulse without ever looking like it is going out

tests.name: ONE period explains the beat on every side of the Dog

detail.note: WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW, said plainly. It shows that a SINGLE period fits the chest, both flanks and the spine seam -- four patches on four sides, one beat. It does NOT establish that their phases are equal: the four passes are taken minutes apart on a clock that advances at the body's ACTIVITY rate, and the phase spread across them came out at 0.49 of a turn, which is what a weak fit over one and a half cycles looks like rather than evidence of four timers. Phase equality is structural instead: DeepBeat and ShallowBeat are two expressions of one Swell, computed once per body per frame in AWonderlandCompanionEmbodiment::AnimateFigure, so the parts cannot drift apart.

tests.name: the pulse survives the Dog walking
